title: PepsiCo Cuts Forecast After North American Sales Slump, Says WSJ Report
body:
PepsiCo announced a downward revision to its full‑year earnings outlook on Thursday, citing a sluggish North American market that has been weighed down by persistent inflation, rising advertising expenditures and softer demand for its core snack and beverage lines. The company reported a 5.6 % rise in net revenue to $25.27 billion for the fiscal third quarter, yet the growth was insufficient to offset the broader headwinds that have eroded profit margins and forced management to temper expectations for 2024.

The earnings downgrade comes as PepsiCo’s North American segment—responsible for roughly two‑thirds of its total sales—registered a notable dip in comparable‑sales growth. While the broader portfolio, which includes global brands such as Lay’s, Doritos, Gatorade and Pepsi, continued to post modest top‑line expansion, the flagship soda business struggled to regain momentum after years of declining consumption. Analysts point to a combination of higher grocery prices, tighter household budgets and a shift toward healthier alternatives as key factors behind the slowdown. In response, PepsiCo has accelerated price hikes across several categories, but the moves have been partially offset by increased promotional activity aimed at retaining price‑sensitive shoppers.

Advertising spend also surged in the quarter, rising to an estimated $2.4 billion, up from $2.1 billion a year earlier. The company has been channeling more dollars into digital and social media campaigns to appeal to younger consumers, while also investing heavily in sports sponsorships and experiential marketing. Although these initiatives are intended to bolster brand relevance, they have squeezed operating margins at a time when cost‑of‑goods pressures from raw material inflation remain elevated. The net effect was a 2.32 % increase in earnings per share, but the growth fell short of the market consensus, prompting investors to reassess the company’s profitability trajectory.

PepsiCo’s strategic pivot toward higher‑margin, “growth‑engine” categories such as premium snacks, functional beverages and e‑commerce fulfillment is already bearing fruit in other regions. International markets, especially in Asia‑Pacific and Latin America, posted double‑digit revenue gains, driven by localized product launches and a stronger focus on healthier snack options. However, the company acknowledged that the North American slowdown could linger, given the lingering effects of a tight labor market and ongoing supply‑chain disruptions that have kept input costs high.

In its earnings call, CEO Ramon Laguarta emphasized that the firm remains committed to “delivering sustainable, profitable growth” and outlined a series of initiatives aimed at revitalizing the North American business. These include expanding the “Snackbot” vending platform, accelerating the rollout of reduced‑sugar formulations, and leveraging data analytics to fine‑tune pricing and promotional strategies. The company also signaled that it will continue to explore strategic acquisitions that complement its existing portfolio, particularly in the burgeoning plant‑based and clean‑label segments.

Looking ahead, analysts will be watching closely how PepsiCo balances the need for price discipline with the imperative to invest in brand equity and product innovation. The revised earnings guidance suggests a more cautious outlook for 2024, but the firm’s diversified global footprint and ongoing transformation initiatives could provide a cushion against regional volatility. If the company can successfully translate its international momentum into the North American market, it may yet recover its growth trajectory and reaffirm its position as a leading player in the competitive food‑and‑beverage landscape.
